caption: A hidden bridge over a gap of 3 blocks (6 blocks, 3x1x5): flip the lever on and a row of 3 slime blocks slides out of the side wall into the gap; flip it off and the row slides back flush into the wall, leaving the gap open. How it works: one sticky piston behind the middle of the row pushes it, and slime blocks stick together, so the whole row moves as one. The ground at both ends is obsidian, which slime cannot pull (stone there would be dragged back with the row). Keep the other cells next to the slime row empty: slime drags any block it touches. Slime slows a walker a little (pext).

A hidden bridge with a stone walkway over a gap of 3 blocks (9 blocks, 4x1x5): flip the lever on and a row of 3 stone blocks slides out of the side wall into the gap; flip it off and the row slides back flush into the wall, leaving the gap open. Stone walks like normal ground (no slime underfoot). How it works: behind the stone row is a row of slime blocks, and behind that one sticky piston. The piston pushes the slime row, which pushes the stone row into the gap; coming back, the slime holds on to the stone and pulls it home (stone does not stick to stone, so only the slime can bring each block back). A piston moves at most 12 blocks, so one piston does up to 6 cells of bridge (pext).

Stone walks like normal ground (no slime underfoot). How it works: behind the stone row are two sticky rows, slime then honey (slime and honey do not stick to each other), each with its own sticky piston behind it: one piston moves at most 12 blocks. The pistons push the sticky rows, which push the stone into the gap; coming back, the sticky blocks pull the stone home. The lever stands on an obsidian block between the two pistons and powers both (obsidian, because slime would drag any other block along) (pext).

A hidden 2-wide bridge with a stone walkway over a gap of 3 blocks (38 blocks, 8x2x6): flip the lever on and two rows of 3 stone blocks slide out of the two side walls into the gap, side by side; flip it off and both rows slide back flush into their walls, leaving the gap open. How it works: each wall holds one stone row with a row of slime blocks behind it and a sticky piston behind that (the stone-walkway bridge, mirrored); the two stone rows meet in the middle and stone does not stick to stone, so each side pulls only its own row home. One lever powers both pistons through a line of redstone dust that runs around the near end of the gap, behind the ground there (the dust needs blocks under it) (pext).
